h: The Portion of Moshe Repairs Pride Desire and Anger

p: "Moshe rejoiced in the gift of his portion."
why the holiness of Shabbos is called
more than all the other mitzvos of the Torah;
"Remember the Torah of Moshe My servant"?
is the repair of the first sin;
הָיָה עַל יְדֵי גֵּיאוּת וְתַאֲוָה וָכַעַס
came through pride, lust and anger,
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and therefore the holiness of Shabbos is called
For in the aspect of pride,
we find that he described himself
with the description of utmost lowliness,
כִּי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית יח, כז)
For Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, said (Bereishis 18:27):
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר (תְּהִלִּים כב, ז)
and King David, peace be upon him, said (Tehillim 22:7):
there is still some substance in them.
אֲבָל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר (שְׁמוֹת טז, ז)
But Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, said (Shemos 16:7):
which has no substance at all.
And in the aspect of lust
"And He buried him in the valley
that is, he was the opponent
and the opposite of the kelipah of Baal Pe'or,
the root of the lust for immorality,
as is known from the women of Midyan,
הֵן הֵנָּה הָיוּ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳
"Behold, they were for the Children of Yisrael, etc.,
the essential power of the kelipah of Kozbi,
who was the daughter of the king;
only to make stumble through her
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
that through this they would catch,
the prince of the tribe of Shimon,
נִפְגַּם עַל יְדֵי זֶה כָּל הַשֵּׁבֶט
the whole tribe was blemished through this,
for all the twenty-four thousand who fell
were from the tribe of Shimon.
depends on the heads of the generation.
And also in the aspect of anger
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, was
clean of any trace or hint of it.
when on the surface there appeared
and he went out of his bounds the slightest bit,
a halachah was hidden from him,
specifically regarding the purging of the vessels of Midyan.
And with this they showed him
that one must be careful in this
just as purification and immersion are needed
in the possession of a gentile.
And in the incident of Zimri
one must specifically make use of
the attribute of anger and zealotry;
therefore this halachah was hidden from him:
has no connection at all to him;
and took what was fitting for him.
הָיָה קְבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
the burial of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, was
across the Yarden, in the territory of Gad,
"for there is the portion of the lawgiver hidden";
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Makkos 9b)
which is the kelipah of anger and zealotry.
And therefore there was buried there
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who was entirely clean of this,
